claims.statement: The repository is a private npm workspace monorepo containing `packages/*` and `examples/*`; root build, lint, and test commands delegate to Turbo, whose pipeline builds dependency workspaces before build, lint, and test tasks.

`@webdecoy/node` publishes exactly the root entry point and `./testing` subpath through its export map, builds those two source entry points as CJS/ESM with declarations, and ships `dist` rather than source files.

The core root entry point intentionally exposes the protection SDK, typed decisions, client-IP and edge helpers, fetch guard, shared adapter-policy helpers, local rules, agent verification, detection, and captcha APIs, enabling custom integrations to use core behavior without deep imports.
Express, Fastify, Next.js, and Hono publish only their root package entry point, depend on `@webdecoy/node`, and declare their host framework as a peer dependency.
`@webdecoy/client` is a separate browser package with a root library export and `./global` script export; its browser-targeted build emits an IIFE global bundle in addition to ESM/CJS library output.

The browser global entry assigns `window.WebDecoyCaptcha`, auto-initializes `[data-webdecoy]` elements when the DOM is ready, and starts clearance collection when its script tag supplies `data-site-key`.

`WebDecoy.protect()` runs configured local rules before remote detection; a local denial/throttle is decided without a detection API call, keyless operation returns a local allow when rules permit, only remote non-allow decisions are cached, and exceptions become an allowed `ERROR` decision.

The shared adapter core owns skip-path matching, standard rule-denial response descriptions, and site-honeytoken derive-and-arm policy; it arms the derived tripwire before advertising the path and derives from the API key so replicas compute the same path.

Framework adapters default to monitor mode: they preserve a typed decision for application code while allowing traffic; enforce mode translates shared rule block descriptions into framework responses, and adapter errors fail open unless a host hook supplies a response.

`createFetchGuard()` is the portable WHATWG Request/Response adapter: it constructs metadata and resolves the client IP, returns a decision plus an enforce-mode response when needed, and only rewrites eligible unread HTML responses; Hono wraps this guard and stores the same decision under `webdecoy` and `webdecoyDecision`.

Express and Fastify use framework-specific HTML response hooks for honeytoken injection, while Next.js intentionally exposes a render-side `honeytokenLink()` helper because Next middleware cannot safely rewrite streamed App Router/RSC output.

The edge compatibility gate bundles supplied entries for browser-platform ESM with framework hosts external, so a reachable Node builtin fails; the root command runs it for core, Next.js, and Hono, and invariant tests separately forbid `node:` imports throughout those source graphs.
Edge compatibility is tested by bundling the core public entry and running keyless protection, Web Bot Auth verification, and captcha token issue/verify/replay flows inside an Edge Runtime VM.

The core captcha HTTP factory owns the normalized `/__webdecoy` challenge, verification, score, and token-verification routes; it can persist invisible-score results by browser session in a supplied signal store so later requests can consume them.

Express, Fastify, and Next captcha exports translate their host request/response contracts into the core normalized captcha endpoint interface instead of independently implementing the captcha route policy.

The published `@webdecoy/node/testing` subpath provides request builders, fresh offline/silent harnesses, assertions, and repeat protection; it suppresses API-key network calls unless `allowNetwork` is explicitly true and gives each harness separate rule state.

The bot registry implementation is generated data consumed by local classification; `BOT_REGISTRY` is deliberately re-exported from the public root API, but the generated registry module itself is an implementation artifact.

The private examples are integration consumers rather than publishable APIs: `express-basic` depends on the Express adapter/core, while `captcha-express` adds the browser client, serves its published global subpath, and mounts the Express captcha middleware.
